latest_teacher_action.diagnosis: The initial prompt preserved object presence and the under relation, but it was too loose for hard attribute recognition and exact counting in a crowded scene. 'Spotted flamingos' and 'glass turtles' were mentioned only once, so those attributes were likely visually weak or lost. The row of seven bicycles with seven turtles underneath created a dense composition where instances may have merged or been omitted, causing both bicycle and turtle count failures.
expected_improvement: Stronger attribute binding should make the flamingos visibly spotted and the turtles visibly glass.
A stricter one-to-one layout should improve recognition of exactly seven bicycles and exactly seven turtles.
Negative count clauses should reduce missing, merged, or extra bicycles and turtles while preserving the passed under relation and black bicycle color.
preserve_constraints: Show exactly three flamingos, all fully visible and separate.
Keep flamingos, turtles, and bicycles all present in the image.

previous_plan_error.details: The prior plan relied on a generic scene description. It did not emphasize visual separability enough for fourteen related objects, and it did not reinforce the spotted and glass attributes with strong repeated binding to the specific targets.

latest_teacher_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple side-by-side composition with the three flamingos separated from the bicycle-turtle grid. Make the bicycles and turtles appear as seven clear one-to-one vertical pairs, with each black bicycle directly above one glass turtle. Strengthen attribute wording on the flamingos and turtles, and add explicit negatives against extra or merged instances.
regression_risks: Making the bicycle-turtle area too dense could still merge instances and hurt counting.
Overemphasizing the seven pairs could accidentally weaken the flamingo count unless the three flamingos remain clearly separated.
If glass is rendered subtly, turtle material recognition may still fail unless transparency and reflective glass appearance are made explicit.
repair_constraints: Exactly three flamingos, and each of the three flamingos is visibly spotted.
Exactly seven turtles, each one separate and fully visible.
Each of the seven turtles is made of clear glass with a transparent reflective glass appearance.
Exactly seven bicycles, each one separate and fully visible.
Each of the seven bicycles is black.
Arrange the seven black bicycles in a single clear horizontal row on the right side.
Place exactly one glass turtle directly below each bicycle, forming seven vertical bicycle-over-turtle pairs.
Keep all seven bicycles and all seven turtles countable, with visible gaps between neighboring pairs.
Do not show any extra bicycles or extra turtles, and do not merge or overlap them.
Keep the three spotted flamingos grouped on the left side, separate from the bicycle-turtle pairs.
latest_teacher_action.retry_prompt: A clear simple scene with exactly three spotted flamingos on the left and exactly seven black bicycles on the right. Each of the three flamingos is fully visible, separate, and clearly covered with visible spots. On the right, show exactly seven black bicycles arranged in a single horizontal row, with visible gaps so all seven bicycles are easy to count. Directly underneath each bicycle, place exactly one glass turtle, so there are exactly seven separate glass turtles total, one turtle under each bicycle, forming seven clear bicycle-over-turtle pairs. Each turtle must look like clear transparent reflective glass. Keep every object fully visible, distinct, and not overlapping. No extra bicycles, no extra turtles, no merged objects.

retry_ready_action.diagnosis: The initial prompt preserved object presence and the under relation, but it was too loose for hard attribute recognition and exact counting in a crowded scene. 'Spotted flamingos' and 'glass turtles' were mentioned only once, so those attributes were likely visually weak or lost. The row of seven bicycles with seven turtles underneath created a dense composition where instances may have merged or been omitted, causing both bicycle and turtle count failures.
expected_improvement: Stronger attribute binding should make the flamingos visibly spotted and the turtles visibly glass.
A stricter one-to-one layout should improve recognition of exactly seven bicycles and exactly seven turtles.
Negative count clauses should reduce missing, merged, or extra bicycles and turtles while preserving the passed under relation and black bicycle color.
preserve_constraints: Show exactly three flamingos, all fully visible and separate.
Keep flamingos, turtles, and bicycles all present in the image.

previous_plan_error.details: The prior plan relied on a generic scene description. It did not emphasize visual separability enough for fourteen related objects, and it did not reinforce the spotted and glass attributes with strong repeated binding to the specific targets.

retry_ready_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple side-by-side composition with the three flamingos separated from the bicycle-turtle grid. Make the bicycles and turtles appear as seven clear one-to-one vertical pairs, with each black bicycle directly above one glass turtle. Strengthen attribute wording on the flamingos and turtles, and add explicit negatives against extra or merged instances.
regression_risks: Making the bicycle-turtle area too dense could still merge instances and hurt counting.
Overemphasizing the seven pairs could accidentally weaken the flamingo count unless the three flamingos remain clearly separated.
If glass is rendered subtly, turtle material recognition may still fail unless transparency and reflective glass appearance are made explicit.
repair_constraints: Exactly three flamingos, and each of the three flamingos is visibly spotted.

Arrange the seven black bicycles in a single clear horizontal row on the right side.
Place exactly one glass turtle directly below each bicycle, forming seven vertical bicycle-over-turtle pairs.
Keep all seven bicycles and all seven turtles countable, with visible gaps between neighboring pairs.
Do not show any extra bicycles or extra turtles, and do not merge or overlap them.
Keep the three spotted flamingos grouped on the left side, separate from the bicycle-turtle pairs.
